Commentary.Commentary: Right then, 282 is the target for Zimbabwe. Their bowlers did well and their batsmen have to live up to their responsibility now. It won't be that easy though, as Pakistan's pace and spin bowling attack are nefariously dangerous. The former more so, because the Pindi cricket stadium, especially the pitch today, favours pace heavily. They would be licking their lips and raring to go now. Let's see how it unfolds as the chase is due shortly...

Needless to reiterate that Zimbabwe bowled well, really well infact. Their skipper would be very pleased with their efforts. Barring Mumba and Chibhabha, everyone were very tight on giving away the runs. Chisoro and Muzarabani got 2 wickets each. Raza and Mumba managing 1 apiece. Nothing for Madhevere or Ngarava but they were very economical.

After opting to bat first, winning the toss, Pakistan got off to a slow start and then ultimately lost three quick wickets. The 3rd was Imam-ul-Haq who made a well-composed half ton. After that, they kept losing wickets but Sohail held onto his end, made a fine 71, before departing. And their lower-middle order did well to build further on Sohail's knock to get them to 281/8. Sure, they could have done a lot but given the way, Pakistan's innings was struggling in the middle, Pakistan batsmen did well to finish it fairly well in the end.

A good, disciplined bowling performance from Zimbabwe. Their pacers and spinners did well and never really allowed Pakistan to get away. Given that nearly every Pakistani batsman got off to a start, Zimbabwe have done well not to allow the Pakistani batters to build on that.

Just a couple of replays and they conclude that it is a six as there was contact with the ropes as the fielder attempted to throw the ball back in.
Is that a six? Has the fielder flicked it inside the ropes before contact? No.... SIX IT IS!

But, the keeper, Taylor collects the balls and takes the bails off with a gently underarm throw. The third umpire has been called for. Replays roll in and it shows that Riaz is short. Terrific work from Taylor.

OUT! RUN OUT! Phew, a decision finally! Imam-ul-Haq has been declared out. Haris Sohail was in by half an inch, more than Imam and hence the latter has to depart. Full and outside off, Imam nudges that to short third man. There was no single there but his partner, Haris Sohail, took off for a run. Imam was ball watching and barely responded to the call. He neither said yes nor no. Haris meanwhile steams intowards the striker's end. Imam was outside of his crease a hint, he dives to try to get back in. The throw comes to the keeper who relays it back to the bowler. A simple run-out at the bowler's end. Now, the question is who's out - Imam or Sohail? Multilple angles are in, multiple times checked. Finally, the umpire deems that Sohail got inside the crease first and Imam later, the latter out!

Is there a run-out here? Massive confusion, multiple angles being examined here. Both batters had run to the striker's end but the question is who was in first. The third umpire has been called in and he is having a look at multiple replays. Very complicated it is becoming here, to judge who stays and who goes. IMAM-UL-HAQ IS WALKING BACK!

Missing international cricket amidst this League humdrum? Then worry not, cause it is back! Yes, Pakistan are taking on Zimbabwe in a 3-ODI series and as many T20Is.
